commits: b13087b A session checks the project without TeX for undefined references and citations, names defined twice, missing inputs and unbalanced environments, braces and maths, and sends them as checks after the build's issues
contract:
New event `checks {items}` (session events, `{"type":"checks","session":n,"items":[...]}`): the whole list each time, items shaped exactly as a build result's errors/warnings LogItems: `{type: "error"|"warning", file, line, message, short}` (no `command`/`missing`), sorted by file then line. Sent once after the session opens (`items: []` when nothing is found) and again whenever the list changes: after a save, another app's change, or a rename (the symbol scan, 150 ms later, makes them, off the session's queue, from the cached Facts). Host keeps the last list; it survives builds and cleans.
Example: {"type":"checks","session":1,"items":[{"type":"warning","file":"a.tex","line":1,"message":"This } has nothing to close.","short":"This } has nothing to close."},{"type":"warning","file":"main.tex","line":2,"message":"No label “nowhere” is defined.","short":"No label “nowhere” is defined."}]}

Issue list numbering (session_issue, session_choose_issue): the session's list is the last build's errors, then its warnings, then the `checks` items, in that order; a host numbers its issue list rows the same way and passes that index to `session_choose_issue`; `session_issue {next}` walks the combined list.

`issues` event lines for an open document: the last build's issues first, then the checks, through the same per-line grouping, so a build's issue wins its line and a check's message joins that line's `others`. An edit still sends `issues` with `lines: []`; the checks come back (in a new `issues` event) after the save's scan. A document edited since the checks' scan began isn't marked with them.

What is checked (only in files the main file reaches; nothing without a main file). Warnings: “No label “x” is defined.” for a \ref kin (skipped when xr or xr-hyperref is loaded; lastpage defines LastPage/VeryLastPage); “No citation “x” is defined.” for a \cite kin (\nocite{*} aside), only while every \bibliography/\addbibresource names a project file; “The label “x” is defined already, on line N of F.” and “The citation “x” is defined already, on line N of F.” (named .bib files) at the second place in TeX's reading order; “No file “x” is in the project.” for \input/\include/\subfile/\import/\subimport, unless the installed TeX's ls-R lists x.tex (skipped entirely without an ls-R, e.g. MiKTeX); “This $ is still open where the paragraph ends.” (also $$, \(, \[); “This { is never closed.”; “This } has nothing to close.”. Errors: “\begin{a} on line N is ended by \end{b}.” (at the \end); “\end{x} has no \begin{x}.” (not in a file another inputs); “\begin{x} is never ended.” (at the \begin; not in a file that inputs another). Comments, \verb, verbatim kin (verbatim, Verbatim, lstlisting, minted, comment), escaped \{ \} \$, \begin/\end inside definitions' arguments (\newcommand, \newenvironment, \def and kin), and names made by macros or parameters (#1) are left alone. All documented in docs/core-api.md (Events table `checks` row, `issues` row, session_issue/session_choose_issue rows, Builds and Symbols rules).

New crates/texlocal-core/src/checks.rs: Structure (a scanner visitor for environments, braces and maths, with definition bodies skipped) and check(), which walks from the main file through Input::resolve and reports undefined refs and cites, labels and .bib keys defined twice, missing inputs and structure slips as LogItems sorted by file then line

syntax/scan.rs: Visit gains brace(at, open) and unclosed(group), the latter called where a paragraph's end drops maths; Group::delimited is shared by the scanner and the checks
tex.rs: installed_beside also reads .tex names into Installed.inputs (sorted), and its ls-R test covers them

Session: the symbol scan computes the checks in its spawn_blocking and sends Msg::Symbols{seq, edits, result}; Builds keeps checks and the edit count; checks_done emits `checks` when the list changes (always the first time) and marks issues; mark_issues chains the build's issues then the checks, each gated by its own edit count; choose_issue and next_issue use the combined list (Builds::listed)

Tests: one per check in checks.rs (tables of cases, including the no-false-alarm text and an \end{document} in an included file), and one session test for the event, the ordering, the combined list and lines, and the return after an edit's save; an existing live test now keeps only live_* events, because the opening `checks` event can land among them
